# **Systems Architecture Spec: High-Precision Position-Space AGV Tracking via Continuous Euler Transitions**

## **1\. Executive Summary & Architectural Topology**

Traditional mobile robot architectures rely heavily on high-frequency velocity-command loops (![][image1]). For automated guided vehicles (AGVs) operating in structured environments with absolute position-controlled actuators, this abstraction introduces unnecessary latency, discretization error, and integration drift.

This document defines a **Continuous-to-Discrete (C2D) Trajectory Pipeline** for a skid-steer AGV. The system bypasses standard velocity-based local planners (such as Regulated Pure Pursuit) in favor of an analytical, time-parameterized geometric path. This path is sampled at ![][image2] on the Single Board Computer (SBC) and streamed over a ![][image3] micro-ROS serial link to a Raspberry Pi Pico. The Pico executes a combined feedforward-feedback position loop.

## **2\. Geometric Curve Modeling (Continuous Space)**

The global route is generated as a ![][image4]\-continuous curve composed of straight lines, circular arcs, and transitionary **Euler Spirals (Clothoids)**.

### **2.1 The Intrinsic Definition**

The defining property of an Euler spiral is that its curvature ![][image5] is directly proportional to its arc length ![][image6] from the origin:

![][image7]where:

* ![][image8] is the spatial odometer coordinate (arc length).  
* ![][image9] is the instantaneous radius of curvature.  
* ![][image10] is the scaling parameter determining the rate of curvature change.

### **2.2 Angular Integration**

By definition, the rate of change of the tangent angle ![][image11] with respect to the arc length is the curvature:

![][image12]Integrating with respect to ![][image6] under the boundary conditions ![][image13]:

![][image14]The heading of the vehicle evolves quadratically relative to the distance traveled.

### **2.3 Cartesian Translation (Fresnel Integrals)**

The differential horizontal and vertical steps along the curve are given by ![][image15] and ![][image16]. Integrating these yields the parametric Cartesian representation:

![][image17]![][image18]Because these integrals are non-elementary, we compute them on the SBC using a highly efficient Taylor Series expansion optimized for local transition segments (![][image19]):

An transition between two opposite turns (S-curve) or a straight-to-bend transition (Spiral-Circle-Spiral) is modeled by composing segments where curvature ![][image22] is continuous at all junction boundaries.

## **6\. Implementation Blueprint (Pseudo-Code)**

This pseudo-code illustrates how the three systems (SBC Profiler, SBC Kinematic Controller, and Pico Firmware) coordinate the C2D pipeline.

### **Module 1: SBC Continuous Trajectory Planner (C++ Class)**

This module fits the continuous Euler transition curves to a path and applies the dynamic time parameterization.

// Header and mathematical types assumed  
struct Pose2D { double x; double y; double phi; };  
struct KinematicState { double s; double v; double a; };

class TrajectoryPlanner {  
private:  
    double max\_vel\_;  
    double max\_acc\_;  
    double max\_jerk\_;  
    double scale\_A\_; // Spiral parameter  
      
public:  
    TrajectoryPlanner(double max\_vel, double max\_acc, double max\_jerk, double scale\_A)  
        : max\_vel\_(max\_vel), max\_acc\_(max\_acc), max\_jerk\_(max\_jerk), scale\_A\_(scale\_A) {}

    // Analytical evaluation of Euler Spiral coordinates at distance s  
    Pose2D evaluate\_euler\_spiral(double s, Pose2D start\_pose, bool is\_left\_turn) {  
        // Taylor series coefficients for Fresnel Integrals  
        double A2 \= scale\_A\_ \* scale\_A\_;  
        double A4 \= A2 \* A2;  
        double A6 \= A4 \* A2;  
        double A8 \= A4 \* A4;  
          
        // Local x, y relative to spiral entry point  
        double x\_local \= s \- (std::pow(s, 5\) / (40.0 \* A4)) \+ (std::pow(s, 9\) / (3456.0 \* A8));  
        double y\_local \= (std::pow(s, 3\) / (6.0 \* A2)) \- (std::pow(s, 7\) / (336.0 \* A6));  
          
        if (\!is\_left\_turn) {  
            y\_local \= \-y\_local;  
        }  
          
        // Heading change is quadratic: phi \= s^2 / (2 \* A^2)  
        double phi\_local \= (s \* s) / (2.0 \* A2);  
        if (\!is\_left\_turn) {  
            phi\_local \= \-phi\_local;  
        }  
          
        // Transform local coordinates into Global Coordinate Frame  
        Pose2D global\_pose;  
        global\_pose.x \= start\_pose.x \+ x\_local \* std::cos(start\_pose.phi) \- y\_local \* std::sin(start\_pose.phi);  
        global\_pose.y \= start\_pose.y \+ x\_local \* std::sin(start\_pose.phi) \+ y\_local \* std::cos(start\_pose.phi);  
        global\_pose.phi \= start\_pose.phi \+ phi\_local;  
          
        return global\_pose;  
    }

    // Time-parameterize the path using a Trapezoidal profile  
    KinematicState sample\_profile(double t, double total\_distance) {  
        double t\_acc \= max\_vel\_ / max\_acc\_;  
        double d\_acc \= 0.5 \* max\_acc\_ \* t\_acc \* t\_acc;  
          
        if (total\_distance \< 2.0 \* d\_acc) {  
            // Short path profile (triangular speed profile)  
            t\_acc \= std::sqrt(total\_distance / max\_acc\_);  
            d\_acc \= 0.5 \* max\_acc\_ \* t\_acc \* t\_acc;  
            double t\_total \= 2.0 \* t\_acc;  
              
            if (t \<= t\_acc) {  
                return {0.5 \* max\_acc\_ \* t \* t, max\_acc\_ \* t, max\_acc\_};  
            } else if (t \<= t\_total) {  
                double dt \= t \- t\_acc;  
                double v\_peak \= max\_acc\_ \* t\_acc;  
                return {d\_acc \+ v\_peak \* dt \- 0.5 \* max\_acc\_ \* dt \* dt, v\_peak \- max\_acc\_ \* dt, \-max\_acc\_};  
            } else {  
                return {total\_distance, 0.0, 0.0};  
            }  
        } else {  
            // Standard trapezoidal profile  
            double d\_cruise \= total\_distance \- 2.0 \* d\_acc;  
            double t\_cruise \= d\_cruise / max\_vel\_;  
            double t\_dec\_start \= t\_acc \+ t\_cruise;  
            double t\_total \= t\_dec\_start \+ t\_acc;  
              
            if (t \<= t\_acc) {  
                return {0.5 \* max\_acc\_ \* t \* t, max\_acc\_ \* t, max\_acc\_};  
            } else if (t \<= t\_dec\_start) {  
                double dt \= t \- t\_acc;  
                return {d\_acc \+ max\_vel\_ \* dt, max\_vel\_, 0.0};  
            } else if (t \<= t\_total) {  
                double dt \= t \- t\_dec\_start;  
                return {d\_acc \+ d\_cruise \+ max\_vel\_ \* dt \- 0.5 \* max\_acc\_ \* dt \* dt, max\_vel\_ \- max\_acc\_ \* dt, \-max\_acc\_};  
            } else {  
                return {total\_distance, 0.0, 0.0};  
            }  
        }  
    }  
};

### **Module 2: SBC 200 Hz Discretization and Kinematics Engine (ROS2 Node)**

This component registers a high-frequency node, performs inverse kinematics, and streams serialized state updates to the serial port.

\#include \<rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp\>  
\#include \<sensor\_msgs/msg/joint\_state.hpp\>  
\#include \<nav\_msgs/msg/path.hpp\>

class KinematicBridgeNode : public rclcpp::Node {  
private:  
    rclcpp::Subscription\<nav\_msgs::msg::Path\>::SharedPtr path\_sub\_;  
    rclcpp::Publisher\<sensor\_msgs::msg::JointState\>::SharedPtr joint\_pub\_;  
    rclcpp::TimerBase::SharedPtr loop\_timer\_;  
      
    TrajectoryPlanner planner\_;  
    rclcpp::Time trajectory\_start\_time\_;  
    bool is\_active\_ \= false;  
    double path\_length\_ \= 10.0; // Dynamic based on path  
      
    // Robot Kinematic Constants  
    const double b\_wheelbase\_ \= 0.45; // meters  
    const double r\_wheel\_ \= 0.10;     // meters  
      
    // Accumulators for wheel targets (Absolute radians)  
    double target\_pos\_left\_ \= 0.0;  
    double target\_pos\_right\_ \= 0.0;  
      
public:  
    KinematicBridgeNode() : Node("kinematic\_bridge\_node"), planner\_(1.0, 0.5, 0.1, 2.5) {  
        joint\_pub\_ \= this-\>create\_publisher\<sensor\_msgs::msg::JointState\>("/pico/joint\_targets", 10);  
          
        path\_sub\_ \= this-\>create\_subscription\<nav\_msgs::msg::Path\>(  
            "/nav2/smoothed\_path", 10,   
            \[this\](const nav\_msgs::msg::Path::SharedPtr msg) {  
                this-\>path\_length\_ \= compute\_path\_length(msg);  
                this-\>trajectory\_start\_time\_ \= this-\>now();  
                this-\>is\_active\_ \= true;  
            });  
              
        // Setup 200Hz Control Loop timer (5.0 milliseconds)  
        loop\_timer\_ \= this-\>create\_wall\_timer(  
            std::chrono::microseconds(5000),   
            std::bind(\&KinematicBridgeNode::on\_timer\_tick, this));  
    }  
      
private:  
    void on\_timer\_tick() {  
        if (\!is\_active\_) return;  
          
        double elapsed\_sec \= (this-\>now() \- trajectory\_start\_time\_).seconds();  
          
        // 1\. Get 1D Spatial State  
        KinematicState state \= planner\_.sample\_profile(elapsed\_sec, path\_length\_);  
          
        // 2\. Map 1D State to Curve Curvature (Mock curve composition geometry for illustration)  
        double current\_s \= state.s;  
        double current\_v \= state.v;  
        double current\_kappa \= 0.0;  
          
        // Compute instantaneous curvature  
        if (current\_s \< 2.5) { // Entering Euler transition  
            current\_kappa \= current\_s / (2.5 \* 2.5);   
        } else if (current\_s \>= 2.5 && current\_s \< 7.5) { // Constant Arc section  
            current\_kappa \= 1.0 / 2.5;   
        } else if (current\_s \>= 7.5 && current\_s \<= 10.0) { // Exiting Euler transition  
            current\_kappa \= (10.0 \- current\_s) / (2.5 \* 2.5);  
        }  
          
        // Compute tangent angular velocity  
        double current\_omega \= current\_kappa \* current\_v;  
          
        // 3\. Compute Differential Inverse Kinematics  
        double omega\_left \= (current\_v \- (b\_wheelbase\_ / 2.0) \* current\_omega) / r\_wheel\_;  
        double omega\_right \= (current\_v \+ (b\_wheelbase\_ / 2.0) \* current\_omega) / r\_wheel\_;  
          
        // 4\. Integrate Positions (dt \= 0.005s)  
        target\_pos\_left\_ \+= omega\_left \* 0.005;  
        target\_pos\_right\_ \+= omega\_right \* 0.005;  
          
        // 5\. Serialize and Publish to micro-ROS Agent  
        auto target\_msg \= sensor\_msgs::msg::JointState();  
        target\_msg.header.stamp \= this-\>now();  
        target\_msg.name \= {"left\_wheel", "right\_wheel"};  
        target\_msg.position \= {target\_pos\_left\_, target\_pos\_right\_};  
        target\_msg.velocity \= {omega\_left, omega\_right};  
          
        joint\_pub\_-\>publish(target\_msg);  
          
        if (state.s \>= path\_length\_ && state.v \<= 0.01) {  
            is\_active\_ \= false; // Path terminal condition met  
        }  
    }  
      
    double compute\_path\_length(const nav\_msgs::msg::Path::SharedPtr msg) {  
        double dist \= 0.0;  
        for (size\_t i \= 1; i \< msg-\>poses.size(); \++i) {  
            double dx \= msg-\>poses\[i\].pose.position.x \- msg-\>poses\[i-1\].pose.position.x;  
            double dy \= msg-\>poses\[i\].pose.position.y \- msg-\>poses\[i-1\].pose.position.y;  
            dist \+= std::sqrt(dx\*dx \+ dy\*dy);  
        }  
        return dist;  
    }  
};

### **Module 3: Raspberry Pi Pico micro-ROS Controller (C++ Bare-Metal / FreeRTOS)**

This logic executes directly on the Pico, consuming raw targets and processing them through a combined Feedforward \+ PID loop.

\#include \<rcl/rcl.h\>  
\#include \<sensor\_msgs/msg/joint\_state.h\>  
\#include "pico/stdlib.h"  
\#include "hardware/pwm.h"

// Hardware Constants  
const float GEAR\_RATIO \= 30.0f;  
const float ENCODER\_RESOLUTION \= 2048.0f; // pulses per revolution  
const float RAD\_TO\_TICKS \= (ENCODER\_RESOLUTION \* GEAR\_RATIO) / (2.0f \* 3.14159265f);

// Loop Tuning Parameters  
const float Kp \= 1.2f;  
const float Ki \= 0.05f;  
const float Kd \= 0.01f;  
const float Kf \= 1.0f; // Velocity Feedforward Gain

// Volatile state variables updated via Serial ISR  
volatile float target\_pos\_L \= 0.0f;  
volatile float target\_vel\_L \= 0.0f;  
volatile float target\_pos\_R \= 0.0f;  
volatile float target\_vel\_R \= 0.0f;

// Error integrals for PI  
float err\_integral\_L \= 0.0f;  
float err\_integral\_R \= 0.0f;  
float prev\_err\_L \= 0.0f;  
float prev\_err\_R \= 0.0f;

// micro-ROS Callback  
void subscription\_callback(const void \* msin) {  
    const sensor\_msgs\_\_msg\_\_JointState \* msg \= (const sensor\_msgs\_\_msg\_\_JointState \*)msin;  
      
    // Extract target positions and feedforward velocities  
    target\_pos\_L \= msg-\>position.data\[0\];  
    target\_pos\_R \= msg-\>position.data\[1\];  
      
    target\_vel\_L \= msg-\>velocity.data\[0\];  
    target\_vel\_R \= msg-\>velocity.data\[1\];  
}

// 1 kHz Hardware Control Timer Interrupt  
bool control\_loop\_callback(struct repeating\_timer \*t) {  
    // Read local encoder hardware registers (mock functions)  
    float current\_pos\_L \= read\_encoder\_left\_rad();   
    float current\_pos\_R \= read\_encoder\_right\_rad();  
      
    // \--- CONTROL MOTOR LEFT \---  
    float err\_L \= target\_pos\_L \- current\_pos\_L;  
    err\_integral\_L \+= err\_L \* 0.001f;  
    float derivative\_L \= (err\_L \- prev\_err\_L) / 0.001f;  
    prev\_err\_L \= err\_L;  
      
    // Combined Feedforward (Velocity) \+ Feedback (PID Position)   
    float u\_L \= (Kf \* target\_vel\_L) \+ (Kp \* err\_L) \+ (Ki \* err\_integral\_L) \+ (Kd \* derivative\_L);  
    apply\_motor\_pwm\_left(u\_L);  
      
    // \--- CONTROL MOTOR RIGHT \---  
    float err\_R \= target\_pos\_R \- current\_pos\_R;  
    err\_integral\_R \+= err\_R \* 0.001f;  
    float derivative\_R \= (err\_R \- prev\_err\_R) / 0.001f;  
    prev\_err\_R \= err\_R;  
      
    float u\_R \= (Kf \* target\_vel\_R) \+ (Kp \* err\_R) \+ (Ki \* err\_integral\_R) \+ (Kd \* derivative\_R);  
    apply\_motor\_pwm\_right(u\_R);  
      
    return true; // Keep timer active  
}

int main() {  
    stdio\_init\_all();  
      
    // micro-ROS hardware and node setup boilerplate omitted ...  
    // rclc\_subscription\_init\_default(\&subscriber, \&node, ROSIDL\_GET\_MSG\_TYPE\_SUPPORT(sensor\_msgs, msg, JointState), "/pico/joint\_targets");  
      
    // Setup a high-priority 1 kHz hardware timer to handle the PID loop  
    struct repeating\_timer timer;  
    add\_repeating\_timer\_us(-1000, control\_loop\_callback, NULL, \&timer);  
      
    while(1) {  
        // Handle background serial polling and micro-ROS executors  
        rclc\_executor\_spin\_some(\&executor, RCL\_MS\_TO\_NS(10));  
    }  
}

## **7\. Performance & Safety Protections**

1. **Safety Watchdog (Heartbeat loss):** If the Pico does not receive a JointState message within a ![][image72] window, the background execution loop must trigger a deceleration routine to bring the AGV to a controlled stop, preventing open-loop runaway.  
2. **Integral Windup Protection:** For heavy-load tracking, clamp the feedback accumulator parameters: err\_integral\_L \= clamp(err\_integral\_L, \-LIMIT, LIMIT).  
3. **Hardware Trajectory Scaling:** If the tracking error exceeds a spatial threshold (e.g., ![][image73]), the Pico must report a tracking fault up to ROS2 via diagnostic topics, stopping the SBC's trajectory timer.

## **8\. Firmware Code Integration**

### **8.1 The "Hacked" Velocity Controller (Legacy Fallback)**
The original firmware utilized a manual `cmd_vel` ingestion model. This ingestion mechanism still remains actively supported, where the MCU applies its own kinematic smoothing and limits to ensure safety during manual joystick operation. This is handled by `drive_process()` in the `DRIVE_STATE_DRIVING` state:

```c
// legacy manual ingestion in drive.c
if (drv->state.enabled && drv->state.last_cmd.id != drv->control.cmd.id) {
    float lin_speed_mm_s = LIMIT_RANGE(drv->control.cmd.linear_speed_mm_s, ...);
    float rot_speed_rad = LIMIT_RANGE(drv->control.cmd.rotational_speed_mrad_s, ...);
    // Kinematic smoothing applied here
    if (drv->state.target_speed_mm_s[i] >= 0 && drv->state.current_speed_mm_s[i] < drv->state.target_speed_mm_s[i]){
        drv->state.current_speed_mm_s[i] += accel_step;
    }
}
```

### **8.2 New High-Frequency State: DRIVE_STATE_EXTERNAL_TRAJ**
To integrate the 200 Hz Position-Space trajectory, a new strict state `DRIVE_STATE_EXTERNAL_TRAJ` was created. When the trajectory subscriber receives `sensor_msgs/msg/JointState` over pico-ROS (Zenoh Pico), it bypasses the manual `cmd_vel` limits and injects raw position and velocity feedforward directly into the control loop.

**Payload Specifications:**
- **Frequency:** 200 Hz (Every 5 ms)
- **Message Type:** `sensor_msgs/msg/JointState`
- **Total Payload Size:** ~106 Bytes
- **Bandwidth Utilization:** ~20% of the 1 Mbit/s serial UART link

```c
// New trajectory integration in drive.c
if (drv->state.sm_state == DRIVE_STATE_EXTERNAL_TRAJ) {
    if ((timer_get_time_us(drv->state.last_cmd_timer) / 1000) > drv->control.joint_cmd.valid_ms) {
        drv->state.sm_state = DRIVE_STATE_STOPPED; // 50ms Watchdog safety
    } else {
        for (int i = 0; i < DRIVE_N_MOTORS; i++) {
            // Bypass kinematic smoothers; track pure trajectory
            drv->state.target_rad[i] = drv->control.joint_cmd.pos_rad[i];
            // Feedforward mapping can be done here.
        }
        drive_set_motor_targets(drv);
    }
    return; // Exit early to bypass linear/rotational ramp filters
}
```

```c
// Subscriber in thread_communication.c
void sub_trajectory_cb(uint8_t *payload, size_t len) {
    static drive_joint_cmd_t cmd = {.valid_ms = TRAJ_TIMEOUT_MS};
    ros_JointState joint_state = {};
    // ... Dynamic sequence buffers allocated here ...
    ps_deserialize(payload, &joint_state, len);
    
    for (int i = 0; i < DRIVE_N_MOTORS; i++) {
        cmd.pos_rad[i] = (float)joint_state.position.data[i];
        cmd.vel_rad_s[i] = (float)joint_state.velocity.data[i];
        cmd.effort_nm[i] = (float)joint_state.effort.data[i];
    }
    drive_set_joint_command(&mcb.drive, &cmd);
}
```

This ensures that the MCU acts as a high-precision servo to the SBC, maintaining flawless $G^2$-Continuous clothoid execution.
